title: Naga administrator named LTO chief; Lacanilao to Marina
summary: The administrator of Naga City has been named new chief of the Land Transportation Office, replacing Markus Lacanilao who has been given a “bigger” assignment as administrator of the…

blocks.text: Noreen Bernadette San Luis and Markus Lacanilao

MANILA, Philippines — The administrator of Naga City has been named new chief of the Land Transportation Office (LTO), replacing Markus Lacanilao who has been given a “bigger” assignment as administrator of the Maritime Industry Authority (MARINA), Malacañang said yesterday.

At a press conference, Palace press officer Claire Castro announced the appointment of former Naga City administrator Noreen Bernadette San Luis as LTO chief and Lacanilao as MARINA administrator, as part of leadership changes in the transport sector aimed at ensuring faster movement of goods as well as safer and comfortable travel for commuters.
“Since former Asec. Markus Lacanilao delivered a good performance and a good message against corruption in LTO, a bigger mission was given to him by the President,” Castro said.

“His appointment as administrator of MARINA is a recognition of his competence because MARINA is at the heart of an industry of 24,000 registered ships and 82 million passenger trips by sea every year,” she added.
“I’m ready, I’m all packed up,” Lacanilao told dzMM after the Palace announcement. Transport group Manibela said its members will continue their strike today to protest the LTO leadership change.

Marcos also appointed Jorjette Aquino as general manager of the Philippine National Railways. Aquino is a former undersecretary of the Presidential Communications Office (PCO), the lead communications arm of the government.

Two key appointees, meanwhile, took their oaths before Marcos yesterday. The President sworn in Douglas Michael Mallillin as chairman of the Commission on Audit (COA) and Maria Angela Ignacio as the new president and chief executive officer of the Maharlika Investment Corp., which manages the country’s sovereign wealth fund.

“The new appointments put two important institutions at the forefront of protecting public resources, promoting accountability and ensuring that government investments contribute to the country’s economic development,” the PCO said in a statement.

Before his appointment as COA commissioner, Mallillin was Director IV under the Office of the Chairperson. A lawyer and certified public accountant, Mallillin was also deputy commissioner at the National Telecommunications Commission, associate prosecutor at the Department of Justice and private legal practitioner at the Edgar M. Avila Law Office. The newly appointed COA chief also taught taxation, business law, accounting and criminal law at St. Louis University and Tarlac State University.
Prior to her appointment to Maharlika, Ignacio was an undersecretary of the finance department.

She was also an undersecretary at the Office of the Special Assistant to the President for Investment and Economic Affairs and managing director of Avisez Asia and of Polestrom. Ignacio also worked as commissioner of the Governance Commission for Government-Owned or Controlled Corporations.
